newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Henderson Inv faces tough 1997 - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Henderson Inv faces tough 1997 - analysts.

text.p: Henderson Investment Ltd faces a tough year in fiscal 1997, with its land bank almost depleted and an asset reshuffle a vital requirement to ensure earnings growth in years ahead, analysts said on Thursday.
The investment holding and property development firm posted fiscal 1996 earnings of HK$1.89 billion on Wednesday compared to HK$1.63 billion the previous year.
The results were below analysts' expectations and Henderson Investment shares closed the morning down HK$0.20 at HK$7.95.

"1997 is the problem year," said Andrew Taylor, analyst at Asia Equity. He had forecast profit for the year ended June 30 of HK$1.94 billion and said net profit looked set to decline to HK$1.83 billion in fiscal 1997.

"The quality of their land bank certainly diminishes from now on and I would be looking at some sort of investment property injection into Henderson Investment to cover the dip in earnings," said Taylor.
Henderson Investment said barring any unforeseen circumstances, its "performance in the coming financial year will show growth over that of the previous year."
Taylor said the firm may produce exceptional gains during the period to achieve positive growth, but added "we still have to see some decent earnings from what is not yet apparent."

Simon Lo, analyst at Kerry Securities, also expected a drop in fiscal 1997 earnings. He said he had lowered his 1996/97 net profit estimate to about HK$1.58 billion from HK$2.2 billion after Wednesday's earnings announcement.
"Developmental projects will not be that great," he said.
Analysts said they expected Henderson Investment's land bank to run out during 1998.

"I think after fiscal year 1996 the size of this land bank is only limited to 530,000 square feet so we expect the land bank should be exhausted by 1998," said Edward Chan, research director at Standard Chartered Securities.

"For the time being, property development contributes about 50 percent of the group's profit so it looks like the Henderson group will inject certain property assets into Henderson Investment to boost its organic growth in the longer term."

Chan expected Henderson Investment to post 2.0 percent growth in fiscal 1997 net profit to HK$1.9 billion. He said if the company had no further property projects in 1998, net profit would drop to about HK$1.8 billion.
Franklin Lam, director of research at HG Asia, said Henderson Investment had a number of options available.
"They will be sitting on considerable cash - the more units they sell more the cash will go up. Just by putting money in the bank there will be recurrent earnings," he said.

"Henderson management generally is very proactive and I do expect them to put top priority on sourcing new projects to seek earnings growth in 1998 and beyond. I do expect some surprises to come out of the group on the acquisition side in the next few months," Lam said.
Taylor said Henderson Investment also had a HK$4.2 billion loan facility "of which I do not believe they have drawn down a lot". He said that would give them scope to acquire assets.
Kerry's Lo said he expected Henderson Land to inject some Chinese infrastructure projects into its unit.

"I expect the management will do some restructuring either by injecting more developmental sites or injecting some China infrastructure projects into Henderson Investment. I believe it will be China infrastructure," he said.
While Lam said he would lower his recommendation on Henderson Investment to hold from buy, Standard Chartered's Chan said he was maintaining a buy rating
"It has just entered into the Hang Seng index and within the context of the conglomerate stocks, it is still trading at a discount in terms of pricing," he said.
